newsitem.title: ITALY: Prosecutors want Mafia probe of Berlusconi dropped.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutors want Mafia probe of Berlusconi dropped.

text.p: Prosecutors in Sicily have asked justice authorities to drop a probe into former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi over alleged Mafia ties on grounds of insufficient evidence, Italian judicial sources said on Monday.
They said prosecutor Guido Lo Forte lodged his written request last week with court officials in the Sicilian capital.
The evidence gathered during the preliminary investigation was "not sufficient to support a court case", one source quoted his request as saying.
The request will be considered by an examining judge.
Media mogul Berlusconi, prime minister for seven stormy months in 1994, is on trial in two separate cases of alleged corruption in Milan. He denies all wrongdoing.
Palermo prosecutors have never confirmed they were probing Berlusconi for alleged Mafia ties, although the investigation had been widely reported in the Italian media.

Last month, Palermo prosecutors asked for the former head of his Publitalia advertising company, Marcello Dell'Utri, to be tried on charges of criminal association with the Mafia. The request is awaiting a decision.
Mafia turncoats have alleged that Dell'Utri, a Sicilian, had acted as a go-between for the Mafia and businessmen in Milan since the mid-1970s. Dell'Utri denies the allegations.
